newsitem.title: CANADA: Telesat says satellite to cost C$350 mln.
newsitem.headline: Telesat says satellite to cost C$350 mln.

text.p: Telesat Canada Ltd said on Thursday it expected its new direct broadcast satellite to require investment of more than C$350 million to build and launch.
"The satellite program that's being built is in excess of C$350 million," Telesat spokesman Paul Bush told reporters. "It's a major undertaking, that's for sure."
The Canadian government said earlier on Thursday that Telesat Canada was awarded one of Canada's prime direct broadcast satellite orbital positions.
Telesat was cooperating with part owner Spar Aerospace Ltd, which won a substantial subcontract from the project, Bush said.
COM DEV International Ltd and U.S.-based Lockheed Martin Corp, would also contribute substantially to the project, Bush said, but he did not know by how much.
The companies plan to build and launch a high-powered 32-transponder DBS satellite into Canada's 91 degree WL orbital slot. The project should be completed by September 1998, Bush said.
Telesat was the only company to apply to build a satellite in the slot, Industry Minister John Manley told reporters on Thursday.
Canada has five more slots, two of which are prime, he said. But he would not say when the other slots would be open for bidding.
"I think it will depend on the market and on the future of the relationship bilaterally with the U.S. on the use of satellites," he said.
The Telesat DBS satellite would provide ample room for all the Canadian companies that expressed interest in supplying direct-to-home television services so far, Manley said.
Telesat is 95 percent-owned by Stentor, the telephone consortium led by BCE Inc unit Bell Canada, and five percent by Toronto-based Spar.
